capitals.name: Chavín de Huántar
capitals.note: The page gives no capital: it calls the site the 'type site'. Ceremonial centre, 3,180 m, Áncash; coordinates approximate, not from the page and not in the gazetteer.

correction.text: the Mosna valley and Conchucos: the core of Chavín civilisation in the northern Andean highlands, Áncash

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -900 to -250: the infobox shows 'the area of the Chavín civilization, as well as areas with Chavín cultural influences' and the page gives the core as the Mosna valley, about 3,150 m, in the northern highlands; Chavín de Huántar page: Áncash, at the confluence of the Mosna and Huachecsa rivers. The influence zone (coast from Piura to Paracas, highlands from Chavín to Pucará) is not drawn as territory. A disc round Huaraz stands in for the Mosna valley (my reading; Huaraz is the nearest gazetteer place).

region.text: the Mosna valley and Conchucos: the core of Chavín civilisation in the northern Andean highlands, Áncash

ledger.note: c. 900 BCE: the Chavín culture develops in the northern highlands. Infobox 'Dates: 900-250 BCE'; the intro says it developed 'around 900 BCE'. The Chavín de Huántar page dates building from 'prior to 1200 BC' and most major construction by 750 BC (conflict).

region.text: the Mosna valley and Conchucos: the core of Chavín civilisation in the northern Andean highlands, Áncash

ledger.note: c. 250 BCE: the Chavín culture ends. Infobox and intro give about 250 BCE; the site's religious function 'had ceased prior to 400 BC' and the New Temple was built 500-200 BC (Chavín de Huántar page). Heirs per the infobox: Moche, Lima, Nazca.

certainty.note: A culture of shared religion and iconography; no borders.

sources.title: Chavín culture
sources.note: Dates 900-250 BCE (infobox), Mosna valley core, influence Piura to Paracas and Chavín to Pucará, not called a state, successors Moche, Lima, Nazca.

sources.title: Chavín de Huántar
sources.note: Built from before 1200 BC, most construction by 750 BC, New Temple 500-200 BC, ceremonial use to about 500 BC, Ancash, 14.79 ha.

notes: A culture, not a state: the page never calls Chavín a state, and describes authority 'rooted in a small elite and shamans'; it also calls Chavín de Huántar 'the place of origin of the second large-scale political entity in the central Andes'. The drawn area is only the Mosna-valley core; the influence zone Piura-Paracas and Chavín-Pucará is cultural. Dates conflict (building before 1200 BC; occupation to at least 3000 BC; Old Temple undated; ceremonial use to about 500 BC; culture to 250 BCE). Capital coordinates are approximate and flagged. [Reviewer am-04, 2026-10-19: successor nazca-culture removed: no land passes (the Nazca culture is on the south coast, Chavin ends 250 BCE) and nazca-culture lists no predecessor; the infobox's 'Followed by: Moche, Lima, Nazca' is a cultural succession only]
